```{r setup, include = FALSE}
uv_snapshot = mobgap::mobgap_uv_snapshot()
ok = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true") && mobgap::have_mobgap()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(mobgap)
```

The `mobgap` package wraps the [mobgap](https://github.com/mobilise-d/mobgap)
Python module with `reticulate`. The Python requirements are declared with
`reticulate::py_require()` when the package is loaded, so no manual Python
setup is needed. The code below needs the Python module and internet access
(to fetch the small example data), so it only runs when `NOT_CRAN=true`.

## Loading a dataset

The Python code

```python
ds = TVSFreeLivingDataset(path, reference_system="INDIP",
                          missing_reference_error_type="skip")
```

becomes

```r
ds = mobgap_dataset(path, type = "free_living",
                    reference_system = "INDIP",
                    missing_reference_error_type = "skip")
```

Here we use the bundled example laboratory data instead.

```{r dataset}
ds = mobgap_dataset(type = "example_lab", reference_system = "INDIP")
mobgap_index(ds)
```

## Reference walking bouts and steps

```{r reference}
dps = mobgap_datapoints(ds)
dp = dps[[3]]
ref = mobgap_reference(dp)
ref$wb_list[, c("wb_id", "start", "end", "n_strides", "avg_cadence_spm")]
mobgap_steps_per_wb(ref)
mobgap_total_steps(ref)
```

For the whole dataset, with identifiers attached:

```{r summary}
res = mobgap_reference_summary(ds)
res$totals
```

## Raw accelerometry and step counts

`mobgap_imu_data()` returns raw sensor data for any loaded sensor position. For
datasets with additional sensors (such as a wrist), pass
`sensor_positions` to `mobgap_dataset()` and select them with `position`.

```{r imu}
imu = mobgap_imu_data(dp, position = "LowerBack")
head(imu)
```

Steps can be timestamped and aggregated to any interval:

```{r steps}
steps = mobgap_step_times(dp, ref)
head(steps)
mobgap_steps_by_interval(steps, "min")
```

## Plot

```{r plot}
imu$mag = sqrt(imu$acc_x^2 + imu$acc_y^2 + imu$acc_z^2)
plot(imu$time, imu$mag, type = "l", col = "grey40",
     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Acceleration magnitude (m/s^2)")
abline(v = steps$time, col = adjustcolor("red", 0.4))
legend("topright", legend = c("acceleration", "reference steps"),
       col = c("grey40", "red"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```


## Comparing with `stepcount` (wrist-worn data)

[`stepcount`](https://github.com/jhuwit/stepcount) estimates steps from
accelerometry. `mobgap_to_acc()` reshapes `mobgap` raw data (m/s^2) into the
`time`/`x`/`y`/`z` (g) format it expects, and `mobgap_compare_steps()` computes
agreement with the reference steps.

```r
acc = mobgap_to_acc(mobgap_imu_data(dp, "LowerBack"))   # keeps attr "sample_rate"
sc  = stepcount::stepcount(acc, sample_rate = attr(acc, "sample_rate"))
mobgap_compare_steps(mobgap_step_times(dp), sc$steps, interval = 10,
                     origin = sc$steps$time[1])
```

Python note: `stepcount` pins `pandas==2.0.*` while `mobgap`/`multigait` need
newer pandas, so run them in separate R sessions. The results below were
precomputed by `data-raw/stepcount-example.R` and stored in
`inst/extdata/stepcount_example.rds`: (a) `stepcount` on the 40-minute
wrist-worn recording `multigait::wrist_imu`, and (b, c) `stepcount` against the
INDIP reference for the lower-back lab example (a rough check, since the models
are trained on wrist data).

```{r stepcount, fig.height = 7}
ex = readRDS(system.file("extdata/stepcount_example.rds", package = "mobgap"))
wrist = ex$wrist_stepcount
cmp = mobgap_compare_steps(
  data.frame(time = ex$lab_reference$time, n_steps = 1), ex$lab_stepcount,
  interval = 10, origin = ex$lab_stepcount$time[1]
)
op = par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
per_min = tapply(wrist$steps, floor(as.numeric(wrist$time) / 60) * 60, sum)
barplot(per_min, col = "steelblue", border = NA, names.arg = NA,
        main = "(a) stepcount on wrist-worn data", ylab = "Steps per minute",
        xlab = "Minute of the 40-minute recording")
barplot(rbind(cmp$data$reference, cmp$data$estimate), beside = TRUE,
        col = c("red", "grey50"), border = NA,
        main = "(b) Lab example: INDIP reference vs stepcount",
        ylab = "Steps per 10 s", xlab = "10 s window")
legend("topright", c("reference", "stepcount"), fill = c("red", "grey50"),
       bty = "n")
plot(cmp$data$mean, cmp$data$difference, pch = 19,
     ylim = range(c(cmp$data$difference, cmp$summary$loa_lower, cmp$summary$loa_upper)),
     main = "(c) Bland-Altman", xlab = "Mean steps", ylab = "stepcount - reference")
abline(h = c(cmp$summary$bias, cmp$summary$loa_lower, cmp$summary$loa_upper),
       lty = c(1, 2, 2))
par(op)
round(cmp$summary, 2)
```

## Getting the Mobilise-D TVS data (wrist and steps)

The full dataset is on Zenodo,
[record 15861907](https://zenodo.org/records/15861907)
([doi:10.5281/zenodo.15861907](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15861907)),
version 1.0.2, licensed **CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0** (check that your use complies). It
is one zip per cohort (HA, MS, PFF, PD, COPD, CHF), each **7-11 GB** (about
58 GB in total), so start with one cohort and check your disk space (zip plus
unzipped).

```r
mobgap_tvs_cohorts()                      # files, sizes, MD5 checksums

# downloads, verifies the MD5, unzips; returns the folder to use as `path`
path = mobgap_tvs_download("~/mobgap_tvs", cohorts = "HA")
```

This creates `path/<cohort>/<participant>/{Laboratory,Free-living}/data.mat`,
which is the layout `mobgap`'s TVS datasets read. Interrupted downloads can be
resumed by calling the function again (valid zips are reused). If you download
the zips by hand from Zenodo, unzip every cohort into one folder and use that
folder as `path`.

Then load the wrist sensor with reference steps. A participant wears the unit
on one wrist, so run each side and combine:

```r
ds = mobgap_wrist_dataset(path, type = "lab", side = "left")      # or "free_living", "right"
dp = mobgap_datapoints(ds)[[1]]
x = mobgap_wrist_steps(dp)
x$imu       # raw wrist acceleration (m/s^2); attr(x$imu, "sample_rate") is 100
x$steps     # reference steps (initial contacts) with clock times
x$wb_list   # walking bouts
```

Example output for one healthy-adult laboratory recording (simulated daily
activities, left wrist):

```
sample_rate: 100   n_samples: 25784   n_steps: 32
mobgap_gravity_means(x$imu[, c("acc_x", "acc_y", "acc_z")])
#> acc_x acc_y acc_z
#>  7.85 -3.61 -2.51
```

`participant_information.xlsx` is not part of the zips; it is only needed for
`mobgap`'s participant-information properties, not for raw data or steps.

## Sensor axes and orientation

Step-counting and gait models that read the raw `x`/`y`/`z` channels are
generally **not rotation invariant**: the same movement looks different if the
device axes, strap rotation or body side differ from the training data. Check
orientation before applying a model to a new device.

```{r orientation}
imu = mobgap_imu_data(dp, position = "LowerBack")
mobgap_gravity_means(imu)                  # gravity should sit mostly on one axis
R = rbind(c(0, 0, -1), c(1, 0, 0), c(0, -1, 0))   # new x = -old z, y = old x, z = -old y
round(mobgap_gravity_means(mobgap_rotate_acc(imu, R)), 2)
length(mobgap_axis_rotations())            # the 24 proper axis rotations
```

Units: `mobgap` returns accelerometer data in m/s^2 (the Mobilise-D `.mat` files
store g); `mobgap_to_acc()` converts back to g.

### Where wrist data and step references exist

`mobgap`'s bundled example data (`LabExampleDataset`) has only the lower back
plus INDIP feet, **no wrist**. Wrist data are in the full Mobilise-D Technical
Validation Study (TVS; see below): version 1.0.2 added an INDIP IMU on the
**left or right wrist** (each participant wore one) for all participants except
CHF5084, CHF5086 and CHF5089, with INDIP initial contacts as the step reference
for both laboratory and free-living recordings.

The notes below on the smaller INDIP sample release
([Zenodo 7802795](https://zenodo.org/records/7802795), CC-BY 4.0; one
healthy-adult in-lab recording with a right wrist) come from an external
analysis and were not re-verified here. The protocol paper (Mazza et al.,
*BMJ Open* 2021;11:e050785) defines a device frame for the lower-back unit only
and gives **no axis definition for the wrist module**, so what the wrist `x`
means in other conventions can't be established from it.

### What an orientation check found (and what it does not show)

| Observation | Status |
|---|---|
| A step model run on the raw wrist channels undercounted by 31% (124 vs 180 steps) and by 52% on the short walking tests. | verified on one recording |
| One of the 24 rotations (new x = -old z, new y = +old x, new z = -old y) gave 179 steps (-0.4% bias, 7.2% per-recording MAPE). | verified, but chosen using the answers |
| In this recording gravity lies almost entirely on `x` (about +1 g) while training sets put it on other axes. | verified |
| The undercount is caused by an axis mismatch. | **inferred, not proven**: strap rotation, forearm placement and the right wrist are confounded |

The best rotation was selected on the same data it was scored on, from 24
candidates, for one person with 180 steps. **Do not quote 7.2% as accuracy, and
do not reuse that rotation without validating on independent participants.**
Prefer rotation-invariant inputs such as vector magnitude, or models trained
across rotations, and validate on more wrist-plus-step participants.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
mobgap_cleanup_uv(uv_snapshot)
```
